parked.name: SEDA (Staged Event-Driven Architecture)
parked.why: Welsh et al. 2001 - a whole-service structure of event-driven stages connected by queues with per-stage admission control; primarily a statement of system-level structure (charter directs it here).

parked.name: Half-Sync/Half-Async
parked.why: POSA2 labels it an architectural pattern: it layers an entire concurrent system into synchronous and asynchronous service layers with a queueing layer between - system structuring, not an in-component mechanism.

parked.name: MapReduce
parked.why: Dean & Ghemawat 2004 - a cluster-scale programming model plus execution framework/topology; the in-program kernel of it is covered by master/worker + pipeline elements.

parked.name: Hardware Abstraction Layer (HAL)
parked.why: Named across beningofw/CMSIS/White as a structural layer of the system, not an intra-component mechanism - Phase 3 architecture realm (bridge target for facade-backend, device-driver, register-access elements).

parked.name: Board Support Package (BSP)
parked.why: System-structure packaging of all board-specific support (simmonds/emb-arch); layer-level construct.

parked.name: Layered software architecture
parked.why: AUTOSAR Classic layered architecture and Noergaard's layered model are canonical architecture-style statements (MCAL -> ECU abstraction -> services -> RTE).

parked.name: Time-Triggered Architecture (TTA)
parked.why: Kopetz-Bauer TTA is a system-level architecture; its in-program counterpart is captured as the time-triggered-scheduler design element.

parked.name: Time/space partitioning (ARINC 653 / IMA)
parked.why: Partitioning of applications across an RTOS/hypervisor is system-level structure (APEX API, Rushby partitioning report).

parked.name: Event-driven architecture (event-driven OS)
parked.why: TinyOS is characterized as a 'tiny event-driven OS' - style-level; the event-loop design element belongs to other scouts' territory.

parked.name: Active-object framework (run-to-completion kernel)
parked.why: QP/QP++ 'active-object / inversion-of-control realization' is framework/kernel-level organization; the Active Object pattern itself is captured as a design element.

parked.name: AUTOSAR Virtual Function Bus / RTE
parked.why: Middleware/communication topology between components - squarely architectural.

parked.name: Microkernel
parked.why: seL4/L4 papers named in emb-arch; OS architecture style, feeds Phase 3.

parked.name: Bootloader
parked.why: Named in zerotomain ('How to Write a Bootloader from Scratch'); a whole-program/system role and boot topology rather than an intra-program mechanism.

parked.name: Small Architecture (Noble & Weir pattern group)
parked.why: The 'small architecture' group of Small Memory Software states memory-conscious system structure; its member mechanisms (pools, overlays, compression) are design-level.

parked.name: Service-oriented architecture (AUTOSAR Adaptive ara::com)
parked.why: Report names AUTOSAR Adaptive as 'POSIX-based service-oriented architecture' - style-level.

parked.name: Two-phase commit (2PC)
parked.why: Atomic commit protocol coordinating multiple independent participants across a system - a distributed/system-structure protocol, not a single-component mechanism (Gray & Reuter name it; Phase 3 candidate).

parked.name: Log shipping / replication log (primary-replica replication)
parked.why: Reuses the WAL as a system-level replication channel between nodes - statement of system structure, feeds Phase 3 (named in Kleppmann DDIA).

parked.name: Shared-nothing parallel database architecture
parked.why: Whole-system partitioning/topology decision (Stonebraker 1986 'The Case for Shared Nothing') - clearly architecture realm.

parked.name: Partitioning / sharding
parked.why: Distribution of a dataset across nodes is system-level structure (DDIA ch. 6); the in-component analogue (hash partitioning of an in-memory structure) would be a different, unnamed-at-this-altitude candidate.

parked.name: Query optimizer / query planner
parked.why: Named recurring construct but primarily a component role in DBMS system structure (Hellerstein et al. 2007 anatomy) rather than a reusable design mechanism; parked rather than dropped.

parked.name: Layered Pattern (RTDP)
parked.why: System-level organization of the whole software stack into abstraction layers - architecture style, POSA1/RTDP canon.

parked.name: Five-Layer Architecture Pattern (RTDP)
parked.why: A specific whole-system layering template for embedded/real-time applications.

parked.name: Microkernel Architecture Pattern (RTDP)
parked.why: Whole-system structuring around a minimal core plus plug-in services - architecture altitude.

parked.name: Channel Architecture Pattern / Channel Pattern (RTDP ch4, DPESC ch6 base form)
parked.why: Organizes the system as sequential data-transformation channels; the base channel concept is system structure (its safety refinements Protected Single Channel and Dual Channel were kept as design elements per charter).

parked.name: Recursive Containment Pattern (RTDP)
parked.why: Recursive system decomposition strategy - statement about system structure.

parked.name: Hierarchical Control Pattern (RTDP)
parked.why: System-wide distribution of control policy across a hierarchy of controllers.

parked.name: Virtual Machine Pattern (RTDP)
parked.why: Douglass presents it as an architecture pattern (portable system atop an abstract machine); the interpreter mechanism itself belongs to the GoF/language scouts.

parked.name: Component-Based Architecture / ROOM Pattern (RTDP)
parked.why: Whole-system component structuring per ROOM methodology - architecture altitude.

parked.name: Homogeneous Redundancy Pattern (RTDP)
parked.why: System-level replication of identical channels for fault tolerance.

parked.name: Triple Modular Redundancy Pattern (RTDP)
parked.why: Three-channel voting redundancy - system-level safety architecture.

parked.name: Heterogeneous Redundancy Pattern (RTDP)
parked.why: Diversely implemented redundant channels against systematic faults - system-level safety architecture.

parked.name: Monitor-Actuator Pattern (RTDP)
parked.why: Paired actuation and monitoring channels - channel-pair system structure for safety.

parked.name: Safety Executive Pattern (RTDP)
parked.why: Centralized system-wide safety coordinator managing shutdown/recovery across subsystems.

parked.name: Data Bus Pattern (RTDP)
parked.why: System-wide shared communication backbone topology.

parked.name: Broker Pattern (RTDP/POSA1)
parked.why: Intermediary-based distributed system topology - POSA1 architecture canon.

parked.name: Client-Server (DPESC ch1)
parked.why: System-level role topology between requesters and providers.

parked.name: Distributed hash table (Chord/Kademlia/DHT)
parked.why: System-level overlay topology built atop consistent hashing; the routing overlay is a multi-node structure, not implementable inside one component.

parked.name: Sharding / data partitioning scheme
parked.why: System-level data-distribution decision across nodes; the in-process hash-ring structure is cataloged, the cluster partitioning strategy is Phase 3's.

parked.name: Distributed replicated log (Kafka-style commit log)
parked.why: As a cluster-wide ordering/replication backbone it is a topology; the in-process append-only log / WAL mechanism belongs to the persistence scout.

parked.name: Blockchain / Merkle-chained distributed ledger
parked.why: System-of-nodes construct composing Merkle trees with consensus; the Merkle tree itself is cataloged as the design element.

parked.name: Search-engine index tier (index + query fan-out architecture)
parked.why: The inverted index is cataloged; the sharded index-serving tier around it is architecture.

parked.name: Message Broker
parked.why: Central intermediary topology that decouples all senders from all receivers system-wide (EIP); primarily a statement of system-level structure.

parked.name: Message Bus
parked.why: Shared enterprise-wide bus connecting many applications via common channels and data model (EIP); an architecture style, not an in-process mechanism.

parked.name: Channel Adapter
parked.why: Connects an application that was not built for messaging to the messaging infrastructure (EIP); a system-integration topology element.

parked.name: Messaging Bridge
parked.why: Connects two separate messaging systems so messages flow between them (EIP); inter-system topology.

parked.name: Pipes and Filters (integration style)
parked.why: As EIP presents it: system-level composition of processing steps connected by channels; the in-process pipeline/pipes-and-filters idiom is a distinct design-level element for the concurrency/POSA scout.

parked.name: Process Manager
parked.why: Central workflow/orchestration engine maintaining process state across multi-step message flows (EIP); system-level control structure.

parked.name: Routing Slip
parked.why: Itinerary attached to a message driving it through a system-level sequence of processing steps (EIP); trends architectural (dynamic workflow across components).

parked.name: Control Bus
parked.why: Separate management/monitoring channel overlay for administering a distributed messaging system (EIP system management); operations topology.

parked.name: Canonical Data Model
parked.why: Enterprise-wide agreement on a common data format to minimize translator count (EIP); cross-system data governance, not an implementable mechanism.

parked.name: Guaranteed Delivery
parked.why: Persistence-backed delivery quality-of-service of the messaging infrastructure (EIP); a system-level guarantee rather than an in-process mechanism.

parked.name: Durable Subscriber
parked.why: Subscription persistence so a disconnected subscriber misses no messages (EIP); a QoS feature of messaging infrastructure.

parked.name: Datatype Channel
parked.why: Channel-per-datatype organization convention for a messaging system (EIP); a channel-topology design decision, not a mechanism.

parked.name: Integration Styles (File Transfer, Shared Database, Remote Procedure Invocation, Messaging)
parked.why: EIP's root-level styles for connecting applications; pure architecture-realm vocabulary for Phase 3.

parked.name: Application Switching (Noble & Weir)
parked.why: Splits the system into independent executables run one at a time - a statement of system-level structure, not an in-program mechanism (fails altitude test upward).

parked.name: Time-Triggered Architecture (Kopetz)
parked.why: System/network-level computation and communication architecture (TTA, TTP); the in-program TTC scheduler element is cataloged, the architecture goes to Phase 3 (corpus: kopetzbauer).

parked.name: Spatial/temporal partitioning (ARINC 653 / IMA)
parked.why: Platform-level isolation architecture between applications; MPU/MMU enforcement is configuration of system structure (corpus: arinc653, rushby).

parked.name: Layered firmware architecture (driver/HAL/middleware/application)
parked.why: The layering itself is architectural structure; only the HAL interface construct was kept as a borderline design element (corpus: lacamera, beningodesign).

parked.name: Redundant channel structures (TMR, dual-channel 1oo2, homogeneous/heterogeneous redundancy)
parked.why: Replication topologies across channels/processors are system-level fault-tolerance structure (Douglass channel patterns; IEC 61508).

parked.name: Limp-home / degraded mode operation
parked.why: System-level behavioral policy for continuing service under fault (automotive lexicon); the in-program safe-state transition is cataloged instead.

parked.name: Dataflow programming (as a system paradigm)
parked.why: As a whole-system execution paradigm/topology it is architecture-realm; the in-program design elements it decomposes into (collection pipeline, FRP) are cataloged here.

parked.name: Function-as-a-Service / serverless functions
parked.why: Deployment and topology construct ('functions' as unit of system decomposition); architecture realm, Phase 3.

parked.name: Model-View-Controller (MVC)
parked.why: Discussed in GoF chapter 1 as the motivating example, but it is a whole-application/UI structural decomposition (Smalltalk-80 lineage) - fails the altitude test upward; feed to Phase 3. GoF itself decomposes MVC into Observer, Composite, and Strategy, which are cataloged here.

parked.name: Publish-Subscribe (as system topology)
parked.why: GoF lists Publish-Subscribe as an aka of Observer (in-process, IN and folded into the observer entry's aka); pub-sub as a distributed messaging/system topology is architecture-level and belongs to Phase 3 - the name lives in both realms per the mission's same-name-two-realms rule.

parked.name: Abstraction Layer / Hardware Abstraction Layer (Fluent C, Beningo)
parked.why: Fluent C names 'Abstraction Layer' for escaping #ifdef variant hell, but as a platform-spanning layer it states component/system structure - architecture realm (HAL).

parked.name: Self-Contained Component (Fluent C, Organizing Files chapter)
parked.why: Prescribes directory/component structure and dependency direction across modules - code-organization at component granularity, feeds the architecture catalog.

parked.name: Shared-nothing architecture
parked.why: Per-CPU/per-thread sharding scaled to whole-system partitioning (Stonebraker's shared-nothing) is a statement of system structure, not an in-component mechanism.

parked.name: Authoritative server with client-side prediction
parked.why: System-level netcode topology (who owns truth, how clients reconcile) - a statement about multi-node structure, not an in-process mechanism; the in-process piece (snapshot interpolation) is cataloged above.

parked.name: Layered game engine runtime architecture
parked.why: Gregory-style engine layering (platform/core/resources/gameplay) is whole-system structure; encountered while sourcing scene graph, belongs to the Phase 3 architecture realm.

parked.name: Server concurrency models (iterative, process-per-connection, preforked, prethreaded server)
parked.why: Stevens UNP ch. 30 catalogs these as whole-server structural alternatives - system-level structure, not an in-component mechanism; feed Phase 3 (relates to thread pool, Leader/Followers).

parked.name: Kernel-bypass networking (DPDK, user-space network stacks)
parked.why: A restructuring of the whole I/O path across OS/application boundary - deployment/system-structure decision, not implementable inside one component.

parked.name: Split top-half/bottom-half driver architecture (as OS structuring principle)
parked.why: The per-driver mechanism is IN as deferred-interrupt-handling; the kernel-wide layering of all drivers into halves is a statement of system structure for Phase 3.

parked.name: Compilation pipeline (multi-pass compiler structure)
parked.why: The lexer->parser->analyzer->codegen decomposition is a whole-program pipes-and-filters structure - system-level shape, not a single implementable mechanism; its stages (lexer, parser, AST) are cataloged as elements.

parked.name: Protocol layering / encapsulation stack
parked.why: Nesting each layer's PDU inside the next (headers-around-payload) is a system structuring principle for communication stacks; the per-layer framing mechanisms (stuffing, TLV, length prefixes) are the design-level elements.

parked.name: Interface definition language / schema-first contract (IDL)
parked.why: Generating serializers from a shared schema contract (protobuf .proto, ASN.1, CORBA IDL) is a cross-component contract-and-toolchain structure; the wire mechanisms it emits are cataloged individually.

parked.name: Model View Controller
parked.why: Whole-app UI structure splitting an application into model, view, and controller responsibilities - app-structure altitude (PoEAA web presentation family).

parked.name: Front Controller
parked.why: Single handler consolidating all request handling for a web application - app-structure altitude.

parked.name: Page Controller
parked.why: Per-page request-handling structure for a web application - app-structure altitude.

parked.name: Template View
parked.why: Web-presentation rendering structure (markup with embedded markers) - app-structure altitude.

parked.name: Transform View
parked.why: Web-presentation rendering structure (transform domain data element by element into HTML) - app-structure altitude.

parked.name: Two Step View
parked.why: Two-stage page-rendering structure (logical page then formatting) - app-structure altitude.

parked.name: Application Controller
parked.why: Centralized point for application flow/navigation control - app-structure altitude.

parked.name: Transaction Script
parked.why: Way of organizing all domain logic as procedures per request - domain-logic organization, app-structure altitude (PoEAA).

parked.name: Domain Model
parked.why: Way of organizing domain logic as an interconnected object model - domain-logic organization, app-structure altitude (PoEAA).

parked.name: Table Module
parked.why: Way of organizing domain logic with one class per table - domain-logic organization, app-structure altitude (PoEAA).

parked.name: Service Layer
parked.why: Layer defining an application's boundary of available operations - explicitly a layer construct, architecture altitude (PoEAA).

parked.name: Remote Facade
parked.why: Coarse-grained facade over fine-grained objects to serve remote calls - primarily about distribution-boundary structure (PoEAA).

parked.name: Client Session State
parked.why: System-level decision to hold session state on the client - state-placement across tiers (PoEAA).

parked.name: Server Session State
parked.why: System-level decision to hold session state in server memory - state-placement across tiers (PoEAA).

parked.name: Database Session State
parked.why: System-level decision to hold session state in the database - state-placement across tiers (PoEAA).

parked.name: Bounded Context
parked.why: Strategic DDD: explicit boundary within which a model applies - system-decomposition altitude (Evans 2003).

parked.name: Context Map
parked.why: Strategic DDD: map of bounded contexts and their relationships - system-level structure (Evans 2003).

parked.name: Anti-corruption Layer
parked.why: Strategic DDD: isolating translation layer between two systems' models - inter-system boundary structure (Evans 2003).

parked.name: CQRS
parked.why: Command Query Responsibility Segregation - splitting a system's read and write models is an architecture style (Fowler bliki 2011; Greg Young).

parked.name: Event Sourcing (architecture style)
parked.why: The system-wide event-sourced-system style (event store as backbone, projections, replay across services) - the in-component persistence mechanism is cataloged as element event-sourcing.

parked.name: Layers (POSA1)
parked.why: Whole-system structuring into abstraction levels - the canonical architectural pattern.

parked.name: Pipes and Filters (POSA1)
parked.why: Architectural style: dataflow topology of a whole processing system (the in-process pipeline mechanism is a separate, smaller element other scouts may carry).

parked.name: Blackboard (POSA1)
parked.why: Architectural style for whole problem-solving systems with cooperating knowledge sources.

parked.name: Broker (POSA1/POSA4)
parked.why: Distributed-system topology / middleware structure.

parked.name: Model-View-Controller (POSA1)
parked.why: Application-level structuring of interactive systems.

parked.name: Presentation-Abstraction-Control (POSA1)
parked.why: Hierarchy of cooperating agents structuring a whole interactive application.

parked.name: Microkernel (POSA1)
parked.why: Platform/product-line level system structure (minimal core plus extensions).

parked.name: Reflection (POSA1)
parked.why: Two-level meta/base architecture for self-modifying systems - system-level structure in POSA1's formulation.

parked.name: Domain Model (POSA4)
parked.why: Application-scale organization of business logic (Fowler PoEAA origin); statement about whole-app structure.

parked.name: Domain Object (POSA4)
parked.why: Component-partitioning construct for structuring applications around self-contained domain concepts.

parked.name: Shared Repository (POSA4)
parked.why: System integration style: components coordinate through a central data store.

parked.name: Message Channel (POSA4, from EIP)
parked.why: Inter-system messaging infrastructure role; middleware topology.

parked.name: Message Endpoint (POSA4, from EIP)
parked.why: Inter-system messaging infrastructure role.

parked.name: Message Translator (POSA4, from EIP)
parked.why: Inter-system integration role (format mediation between systems).

parked.name: Message Router (POSA4, from EIP)
parked.why: Inter-system routing topology element.

parked.why: Broker-decomposition middleware transport role.

parked.why: System-level replication structure for availability/scalability.

parked.name: Activator (POSA4)
parked.why: On-demand activation of services/processes (inetd-style); deployment/system-level resource mechanism.

parked.why: Web-application structuring pattern; app-level control topology.

parked.name: Front Controller (POSA4, from PoEAA)
parked.why: Web-application structuring pattern; app-level control topology.

parked.why: Web presentation-layer structure; app-structure flavored - a Fowler-focused scout may reclaim it downward.

parked.name: Transform View (POSA4, from PoEAA)
parked.why: Web presentation-layer structure; app-structure flavored - a Fowler-focused scout may reclaim it downward.

parked.why: Network security topology element.

parked.why: Security-architecture pattern (policy enforcement structure across a system); Phase 3 / security territory.

parked.why: Hanmer pattern; switching service to a redundant unit is primarily a system-level structure/tactic (per charter directive: park if system-level).

parked.name: Redundancy (spatial/temporal/informational)
parked.why: Hanmer architectural pattern; provisioning redundant units is an availability tactic / system structure, not an in-program mechanism.

parked.name: Units of Mitigation

parked.name: Error Containment Barrier
parked.why: Hanmer architectural pattern; primarily prescribes structural boundaries for error propagation across the system.

parked.name: Someone in Charge
parked.why: Hanmer architectural pattern; assigns system-wide responsibility for fault-handling actions - structural/organizational.

parked.name: Fault Observer
parked.why: Hanmer pattern; a system-wide component collecting and publishing fault reports - topology-level.

parked.name: System Monitor
parked.why: Hanmer detection pattern; a dedicated monitoring component watching the rest of the system - system-level structure.

parked.name: Maintenance Interface
parked.why: Hanmer pattern; a separate management/maintenance channel beside the application interface - architectural interface decision.

parked.name: Health Check (endpoint)
parked.why: Per charter directive; a service-exposed liveness/readiness probe is a system/operations integration construct (cf. heartbeat, which stays design-level).

parked.name: Decoupling Middleware
parked.why: Nygard stability pattern; choosing middleware topology to decouple systems is architectural.

parked.name: Graceful Degradation
parked.why: System-level quality tactic (SRE / Bass availability tactics); realized by design elements like load shedding and circuit breaker but itself a system property.

parked.name: Process Pairs
parked.why: Gray (1985, Tandem); primary/backup process structure with takeover - system-level redundancy organization.

parked.name: Triple Modular Redundancy (TMR)
parked.why: Lyons & Vanderkulk (1962); hardware/system-level redundancy with voting; software analog covered by n-version-programming element.

parked.name: Saga / Compensating Transaction
parked.why: Garcia-Molina & Salem (1987); long-lived transaction structure spanning services - architecture-level failure handling (flagging for Phase 3; may also belong to a persistence scout).

parked.name: Shed Work at Periphery
parked.why: Hanmer overload pattern; prescribes WHERE in the system to shed load (at the edge) - a placement/topology statement; the mechanism itself is the load-shedding element.

parked.name: Model-View-Presenter (MVP)
parked.why: App-structure variant of MVC (Potel; Fowler's Passive View and Supervising Controller are its sub-variants) - Phase 3.

parked.name: Model-View-ViewModel (MVVM)
parked.why: App-structure pattern (Gossman, Microsoft WPF) built on data binding; the binding mechanism is cataloged as a design element, the structure parks here.

parked.name: Presentation-Abstraction-Control (PAC)
parked.why: POSA 1 architectural pattern - hierarchical agent decomposition of an interactive system, system-structure altitude.

parked.name: Presentation Model
parked.why: Fowler GUI-architecture pattern (2004) - app-structure separation predecessor of MVVM.

parked.name: Flux
parked.why: Facebook's application architecture for unidirectional data flow (dispatcher/store/view) - app-structure altitude; Redux/centralized-store is its best-known descendant.

parked.name: Elm Architecture
parked.why: aka Model-View-Update (MVU); whole-app structure (model/update/view triad) from the Elm guide - app-structure altitude.

parked.name: Unidirectional Data Flow
parked.why: App-wide data-flow discipline umbrella (Flux/Elm/MVI family) - a constraint on system structure, not an in-component mechanism.

parked.name: Model-View-Intent (MVI)
parked.why: Reactive app-structure variant (cycle.js lineage) of unidirectional data flow - Phase 3 with the MV* family.

parked.name: Islands Architecture
parked.why: Page-level structure for partial hydration (Astro et al.); the hydration mechanism itself is cataloged as a design element.

parked.name: Sidecar
parked.why: Azure: auxiliary component deployed as a separate process/container alongside the main application - deployment topology.

parked.name: Ambassador
parked.why: Azure: out-of-process helper proxy for remote communication on behalf of a service - topology.

parked.name: Gateway Aggregation / Gateway Routing / Gateway Offloading
parked.why: Azure: system-edge gateway structures - topology.

parked.name: Backends for Frontends
parked.why: Azure: per-frontend backend services - whole-system structuring.

parked.name: Gatekeeper
parked.why: Azure: dedicated validating host between clients and backends - deployment topology for security.

parked.name: Strangler Fig
parked.why: Azure/Fowler: incremental legacy-system replacement strategy - system migration structure.

parked.name: Queue-Based Load Leveling
parked.why: Azure: queue as buffer between services - inter-service topology (in-process message queue is a separate design element owned elsewhere).

parked.name: Competing Consumers
parked.why: Azure/EIP: multiple consumer instances on a shared channel - system-scale messaging.

parked.name: Publisher-Subscriber
parked.why: Azure: system-scale async messaging topology; in-process pub-sub is covered by Observer/Event Aggregator in the design realm.

parked.name: Event Sourcing
parked.why: Azure: append-only event store as the system of record - data-architecture level (db scout may claim a mechanism-level form).

parked.name: Scheduler Agent Supervisor
parked.why: Azure: distributed action coordination and recovery - multi-service structure.

parked.name: Leader Election
parked.why: Azure: coordination across distributed instances - distributed-systems mechanism above component level.

parked.name: Sharding
parked.why: Azure: horizontal partitioning of a data store - data-architecture.

parked.name: Deployment Stamps / Geode
parked.why: Azure: replicated deployment units / geo-distributed nodes - deployment topology.

parked.name: Federated Identity / Valet Key
parked.why: Azure: cross-system authentication delegation / token-based direct resource access - system-level security structures.

parked.name: Health Endpoint Monitoring
parked.why: Azure: externally-probed health checks - operational/system monitoring structure.

parked.name: Static Content Hosting / External Configuration Store
parked.why: Azure: moving content/config to external services - deployment decisions.

parked.name: Claim Check / Sequential Convoy / Messaging Bridge / Asynchronous Request-Reply / Choreography
parked.why: Azure/EIP system-messaging patterns - inter-service; EIP scout may claim mid-level subsets.

parked.name: Compute Resource Consolidation
parked.why: Azure: packing tasks into deployment units - deployment-level.

parked.name: Index Table / Materialized View
parked.why: Azure: data-tier query structures - data-architecture; db scout may claim mechanism-level forms.

parked.name: Blackboard
parked.why: On Wikipedia's behavioral list but canonically a POSA1 architectural pattern - system-level knowledge-source structure.

parked.name: Half-Object + Protocol (HOPP)
parked.why: PLoP (Meszaros 1995): splitting an object across address spaces with a protocol between halves - distribution structure.

parked.name: Health Check API
parked.why: Richardson (microservices.io) names it, but it is a service-topology observability endpoint contract, not an in-program mechanism; belongs in the Phase 3 architecture realm.

parked.name: Transactional Outbox
parked.why: Reliable event publication across a database + broker boundary; inherently a multi-component reliability topology (Richardson names it); park for Phase 3.

parked.name: Saga
parked.why: Distributed long-lived transaction decomposition with compensations (Garcia-Molina & Salem 1987; Richardson); cross-service coordination topology, not an in-program element.

parked.name: Safety Executive
parked.why: Douglass safety pattern cataloged in Preschern/Kajtazovic/Kreiner 'Building a Safety Architecture Pattern System' (EuroPLoP 2013, ACM 10.1145/2739011.2739028): a centralized safety monitor component coordinating fail-safe shutdown across subsystems - system-level structure, fails the altitude test upward.

parked.name: Monitor-Actuator (channel pair)
parked.why: Douglass safety pattern in the same Preschern EuroPLoP 2013 safety pattern system: separate actuation channel and monitoring channel as distinct components - architecture-level channel structure (index's dual-channel and protected-single-channel cover the in-component mechanisms).

parked.name: Safety tactics catalog (Wu-Kelly, via Preschern's GSN tactic analysis)
parked.why: Preschern's EuroPLoP 2013/2019 safety-pattern-system papers organize patterns under safety tactics (condition monitoring, degradation, replication/diversity redundancy, repair...) - tactics are Phase 3 architecture-realm material; the implementable members (sanity check, watchdog, N-version, dual channel) are already in the design index.

parked.name: Authoritative Server model
parked.why: Client/server with server-authoritative simulation (vs peer-to-peer lockstep) is a system-topology decision, not an in-component mechanism; the in-component mechanisms it induces (prediction, reconciliation, lag compensation) are cataloged above.

parked.name: HLA Run-Time Infrastructure / federated simulation
parked.why: IEEE 1516 federation of simulators is system-level structure; only its interest-management/DDM mechanism passes the altitude test (included above).

parked.name: MV* family (Model-View-Controller, MVP, MVVM)
parked.why: Osmani's JS pattern catalog includes MV* patterns, and none appear in the element index under any alias; they are GUI architectural patterns (POSA1 names MVC an architectural pattern). Parked so Phase 3 verifies the architecture realm covers them - flagged here because their total absence from the design index is conspicuous.

parked.name: Privilege Separation (Provos et al.)
parked.why: Splits a program into privileged monitor and unprivileged worker processes — multi-process system structure, not in-process; distinguished from privilege bracketing (which is in-process and included)

parked.name: Sandbox / process sandboxing (seccomp, pledge, jails)
parked.why: OS-enforced isolation topology around a process, not a mechanism inside it

parked.name: Secure channel / Secure Pipe (TLS)
parked.why: Inter-system communication security infrastructure (Core Security Patterns 'Secure Pipe')

parked.name: Single Sign-On / third-party authentication (Kerberos, OAuth/OIDC topology)
parked.why: Cross-system identity federation topology

parked.name: Demilitarized Zone, Packet Filter Firewall, Proxy-Based Firewall (Schumacher et al.)
parked.why: Network security topology patterns from the same catalog; clearly architecture realm

parked.name: Policy Decision Point / centralized authorization service (XACML PEP/PDP/PIP)
parked.why: Distributed authorization topology; its in-process kernel is covered by reference-monitor

parked.name: Intrusion Detection System
parked.why: Infrastructure component observing systems from outside

parked.name: Secrets management service / vault
parked.why: Infrastructure for credential storage and distribution

parked.name: Defense in Depth / Compartmentalization (as structure)
parked.why: System-structuring principle; layered independent controls is an architecture-level statement

parked.name: Recursive Control (Selic, PLoPD3)
parked.why: Structuring pattern for whole real-time control systems (hierarchy of control components); system-level structure, fails altitude upward.

parked.name: Bodyguard (das Neves & Garrido, PLoPD3)
parked.why: Sharing and protecting objects across address spaces in distributed systems without full RPC; distribution-level.

parked.name: Object Synchronizer (Silva, Pereira & Marques, PLoPD4)
parked.why: Synchronization policy for distributed object replicas; distribution-level.

parked.name: Single Access Point + Check Point (Yoder & Barcalow, PLoPD4)
parked.why: Presented as 'Architectural Patterns for Enabling Application Security'; application-entry security structure, Phase 3 territory.

parked.name: Dynamic Object Model / Adaptive Object Model (Riehle, Tilman & Johnson, PLoPD5)
parked.why: Yoder/Johnson describe it as an architectural style; its design-level constituents (Type Object, Property/attribute objects, Strategy, Interpreter) are already in the catalog.

parked.name: Event Collaboration (Fowler, eaaDev 'Focusing on Events')
parked.why: Components coordinate by broadcasting events instead of making requests — as a cross-component interaction style this is event-driven architecture's territory (Phase 3); its in-process mechanisms are already cataloged (observer, event-aggregator, domain-event, message-queue).

parked.name: Reporting Database (Fowler, bliki 2004)
parked.why: Separate database fed from the operational store for reporting/analytics — system-level data topology, fails altitude upward.

parked.name: Bounded Context (Evans DDD; Fowler bliki 2014)
parked.why: Strategic-design decomposition of a large model/system into contexts with explicit boundaries — system-structure altitude, Phase 3 (belongs with the DDD strategic set alongside already-parked Service Layer etc.).

parked.name: Polyglot Persistence (Fowler/Sadalage, bliki 2011)
parked.why: Using different datastore technologies per data need across a system — data-architecture stance, Phase 3 territory.

parked.name: Distributed Snapshot / Checkpoint Barrier (Chandy-Lamport; Flink Asynchronous Barrier Snapshotting)
Session State placement trio: Client Session State / Server Session State / Database Session State (PoEAA)
